top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a clean, two-laureate achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms is a distinct mechanism from the frequency comb and single-ion control, and fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 have been reproduced by several laboratories, so the result is experimentally secure. It has already enabled new measurements (gravitational redshift over millimetre heights, bounds on drifting constants, many-body clock physics). IceCube is a strong discovery but its three-name cut from a large collaboration and its source identification are less settled; it ranks above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no collaboration with Katori, Ye or the IceCube leaders. Declared measurement-science bias toward the clock case.
